hero.eyebrow: 8 KfW loans. 16 state tax rates. One monthly payment.
hero.lede: Your bank quotes you one number. This shows you the rest: the cheap KfW loans you can stack, the cash you need on the day, and what happens when your fixed rate runs out.

principles.title: You can stack loans, within limits
principles.body: KfW 300 will not sit next to 297 or 298. KfW 261 is for renovations, not new builds. KfW 124 and 270 go with almost anything. Each one has its own ceiling, its own rate and its own conditions.

principles.title: Some of it has to be cash
principles.body: Transfer tax is 3.5% in Bayern and 6.5% in NRW. Add the notary, the land registry and the agent and you need 5 to 12 percent of the price in cash on the day you complete. No bank will lend you that part.

principles.title: Year ten is the one to watch
principles.body: Most fixed rates last ten years. After that, whatever you still owe is refinanced at whatever rate exists then. Try a high one and see whether the payment still works.

faq.q: Why can I not borrow the fees?
paras: German banks lend against the value of the property, and the fees around the purchase are not part of that value. So the transfer tax, the notary, the land registry and the agent all have to come out of your own savings, on top of any down payment.
Expect roughly 5.5 to 8.5 percent of the price without an agent, and 9 to 12 percent with one.

A one off tax when you buy, and usually the biggest single fee. Each state sets its own rate. It runs from 3.5 percent in Bayern up to 6.5 percent in NRW, Brandenburg, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein.

Every sale has to be signed in front of a notary and recorded in the land register. The notary is around 1.5 percent and the registry around 0.5 percent, much the same everywhere. Both are editable above if your quote differs.

faq.q: When do I pay an agent?
paras: Only if one is involved in the sale. Since December 2020 the fee is split about evenly between buyer and seller, which usually leaves your half at around 3.57 percent including VAT.
The down payment is the part of the price you cover yourself, and it lowers what you borrow. Cash needed is that plus every fee, which is the money that has to be in your account on completion day.

A stretch at the start where you pay interest and nothing comes off the loan. Your early payments are smaller, but you then repay the whole loan over fewer years, so the payment afterwards is bigger and you pay more interest overall. The monthly figure at the top of the page is that bigger payment.

KfW loans normally fix the rate for ten years, and the dashed line in the chart marks the end of it. Whatever you still owe then gets refinanced at whatever rate is on offer. Nobody knows that number, so it is worth trying a few.

faq.q: Which KfW loans can I combine?
paras: Some cannot share a home. KfW 300 will not go with 297 or 298, and 297 and 298 are two versions of the same loan so you pick one. KfW 261 is for renovations and does not go with the new build loans.
KfW 124 and 270 go with almost everything, and so does your bank loan. You will see a warning if you pick a pair that is not allowed.

faq.q: Where do these numbers come from?
paras: The ceilings, income limits and combination rules come from the official KfW pages, and each one carries the date it was last checked. The interest rates do not: KfW does not publish them, because your rate is set when your loan is approved. Every rate here is a plausible starting point for you to replace with the one on your own offer.
Rules change. Check the official pages before you sign anything.
Nowhere. Everything you enter, including any changes to the loan list, is saved in this browser only. Start over puts the example numbers back.
